newsitem.title: USA: Indiana soybean harvest advances to 92 percent.
newsitem.headline: Indiana soybean harvest advances to 92 percent.

text.p: Indiana's soybean harvest pace advanced to 92 percent complete during the week ended Sunday, up from 80 percent the previous week, according to the Indiana Agricultural Statistics Service.
That combining tally was below the 100 percent chalked up a year ago and below the 98 percent average pace.
Corn harvest stood at 65 percent complete, above the 47 percent a week ago but below the 96 percent of a year ago and below the 80 percent average pace.
Corn harvest was 11 days behind average and lodging was a serious problem in many corn fields.
Winter wheat seeding was 97 percent complete, up from 88 percent a week ago but below the 100 percent pace of a year ago and below the 98 percent average pace.
Eighty-four percent of the crop had emerged, up from 70 percent a week ago but below the 92 percent a year ago and below the 89 percent average.
Winter wheat was 14 percent excellent, 67 percent good, 18 percent fair and one percent poor.

Topsoil moisture levels were 49 percent surplus, 49 percent adequate and two percent short. Subsoil moisture was 22 percent surplus, 72 percent adequate, five percent short and one percent very short.
